 Politics & Policy Denmark ratifies Trump security deal over Greenland after months of diplomatic tensions
 Published Thu, Nov 19 2026 5:35 AM EST Updated Thu, Nov 19 2026 7:02 AM EST Sam Meredith @in/samuelmeredith @smeredith19 WATCH LIVE Key Points Denmark’s parliament approved a U.S. security agreement covering Greenland, following Greenland’s ratification earlier this month.
 The deal allows the U.S. to expand its military presence in Greenland while maintaining Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders’ right to self-determination.
 It follows months of tensions after Trump repeatedly said the U.S. should take control of Greenland for national security reasons.
 Denmark's Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen (sitting, R) attends the second legislative process and vote on the security agreement between Denmark, Greenland and the US in the Parliament Hall at Christiansborg in Copenhagen, on November 19, 2026. Mads Claus Rasmussen | Afp | Getty Images Danish lawmakers on Thursday approved a security agreement with U.S. President Donald Trump covering Greenland, seeking to end months of strained diplomatic tensions over the island's future.
 Trump and the prime ministers of Denmark and Greenland signed the agreement in September. It allows Washington to expand its military presence on the island, paving the way for two new bases and the construction of a " Golden Dome " missile defense system.
 Thursday's approval follows a protracted period in which Trump repeatedly threatened to take control of the self-governing Danish territory. Tensions reached fever pitch in January as the president repeatedly insisted that the U.S. needed Greenland for its national security, at times declining to rule out using military force to acquire it.
 A parliamentary tally showed 109 Danish lawmakers unanimously backed the agreement on Thursday, per Reuters. Greenland's parliament ratified the deal earlier this month. It is not subject to a vote in the U.S. Senate.
 NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 22: (L-R) U.S. President Donald Trump, Prime Minister of Denmark Mette Frederiksen and Prime Minister of Greenland Jens-Frederik Nielsen hold up the proclamations during the signing of a security pact between the U.S., Denmark, and Greenland during the 81st session of the United Nations (U.N.) General Assembly at U.N. Headquarters on September 22, 2026 in New York City. Chip Somodevilla | Getty Images News | Getty Images The Danish government can now formally notify the U.S. that both parliaments have consented to complete the ratification process.
 The deal supplements an existing 1951 defense agreement. It also maintains Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders' right to self-determination.
 Trump's proposed Golden Dome is a multibillion-dollar initiative designed to shield the U.S. from a range of aerial and missile threats. It was rolled out in May last year and is often compared with Israel's " Iron Dome " system.
 Trump's threats alarmed Greenlanders and other Europeans and opened a rift between the U.S. and NATO, of which Denmark and the U.S. are both members. Greenland has maintained that it is not for sale, and the European Union earlier this year united to rebuke Trump . 
 — CNBC's Kevin Breuninger & Anniek Bao contributed to this report.
